question: Was the Central line between Liverpool Street and Bethnal Green ground to reduce noise, and when?
norm_question: was the central line between liverpool street and bethnal green ground to reduce noise and when

answer.text: In the Mayor's written answer to Question 2022/1791 (28 June 2022), the Central line section from Bethnal Green to Liverpool Street benefitted from rail grinding to help reduce noise between December 2021 and May 2022, though was not on the provisional list for June to November 2022.
answer.review: reviewed in the final check of the revision

verified_claims.text: In the spreadsheet attached to the Mayor's written answer to Question 2022/1791 on 28 June 2022, the Central line section from Bethnal Green to Liverpool Street is listed among the sections that benefited from rail grinding to help reduce noise levels between December 2021 and May 2022.

citations.quote:
Date:
Tuesday 28 June 2022
While the primary purpose of rail grinding on the Tube network is safety and operational reliability by managing rail defects, and maximising asset life, it is also used for the purpose of noise reduction.
The requested information is in the attached spreadsheet.

Bethnal Green to Liverpool Street

verified_claims.text: In the same Mayor's Question 2022/1791 spreadsheet, the provisional and subject-to-change list of sections scheduled for rail grinding between June 2022 and November 2022 did not include Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green, listing only Queensway to Lancaster Gate on the Central line.

citations.quote:

verified_claims.text: Separately from rail grinding, a TfL document on deep Tube reconditioning works listed eastbound Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green on the Central line under deep Tube reconditioning works planned for financial year 2023/24.
